storyboard.claim: A gold's slip of language, bloody dam and reaper scythe, gives away that Titus is a red.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, mid-oath in the hall; no icon, since nothing in the vocabulary reads 'slip of language'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the confrontation in the dark castle hall.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exact slip: a gold would say reaper scythe, a hell diver would say sling blade.

storyboard.claim: Darrow is struck by a chilling realization about Titus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow alone in the dark hall, afraid, thinking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow catches the slip from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the realization landing on Darrow, not just being announced.

storyboard.claim: Titus is not a gold at all but a red wearing a gold face.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask icon reads as a false public face; Titus smirks while Darrow looks on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the slip to what it reveals: Titus is an infiltrator.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask says the gold identity is a disguise, and the smirk says he is enjoying the lie.

storyboard.claim: Titus plays the infiltration as a contest to be won by brutality, not by breaking the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A game icon reads literal game; Titus angry, talking, in the hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains Titus's strategy after his identity is established.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames his method as a game he means to win by force.

callout.text: GOLDS TOOK THE GIRL HE LOVED

storyboard.claim: Titus's origin begins with the Golds taking the red girl he loved and harming her in front of him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, sad and slumped; the harm itself is not drawn.
storyboard.onScreenText: GOLDS TOOK THE GIRL HE LOVED
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from Titus's identity to his backstory.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sad slumped body marks this as the wound behind his cruelty without staging the violence.

storyboard.claim: Titus's mind broke, and he killed the men who wronged her and was taken to the institute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, standing; no icon and no violence drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the backstory: the break and the sons of Aries.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout names the break; the angry face shows the rage that followed.

storyboard.claim: Titus now raids gold houses, taking students and harming the gold girls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, pointing toward the houses; nothing drawn of the harm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the origin to his present campaign.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing at the houses shows the raids are aimed at a specific target.

storyboard.claim: Titus's own words: he believes the gold daughters must suffer what his girl suffered.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, speaking the line to Darrow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Titus says it himself, in the first person.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quote is the revenge logic in his own voice; the viewer hears it from him.

storyboard.claim: Titus sincerely believes his revenge is justice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus with a self-satisfied smirk, talking; no balance icon, since a balance would read endorsement of justice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Judges the quote: Titus thinks what he does is just.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows his self-righteous certainty, the belief the narrator is about to take apart.

storyboard.claim: The hosts turn from Titus's belief to what his actions do structurally.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking to camera; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from Titus's belief to structure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats as the structural analysis.

storyboard.claim: Fighting the oppressor with the oppressor's tools makes you another oppressor and frees no one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram: their tools, then another monster, then no liberation.
storyboard.onScreenText: Their tools Another monster No liberation
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the structural principle behind the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three-step flow makes the cause and effect visible without words.

storyboard.claim: Titus stays inside the oppressive system, becoming one more monster within it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chains icon reads bound and imprisoned, matching the cage; the narrator speaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the principle to Titus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains make the cage literal: he is bound inside the system.

callout.text: A RED OPERATING A GOLD MACHINE

storyboard.claim: Titus is a red soul running the gold machine of domination.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, pointing forward as if commanding a system; no icon.
storyboard.onScreenText: A RED OPERATING A GOLD MACHINE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues: he has taken the dominant position inside the system.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture shows him commanding, not escaping.

storyboard.claim: The machine does what it was designed for: it crushes people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator thinking aloud; no icon, since a crushing machine has no literal icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the machine metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the claim that the system's design is to crush.

callout.text: SEND A WARLORD BEHIND THE LINES

storyboard.claim: A terrorist group would want to send a warlord behind enemy lines to tear the gold society apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon for the warlord and the front; the narrator speaks it as a hypothetical.
storyboard.onScreenText: SEND A WARLORD BEHIND THE LINES
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator's hypothetical: what the sons of Aries would want.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the strategy in a literal military image.

storyboard.claim: Creating chaos is counterproductive; it is not real revolution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; the struck phrase rejects the equation of chaos with revolution.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the hypothetical: chaos is the wrong goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the rejected equation; no icon would show the difference.

storyboard.claim: Dancer, the rebel leader, deliberately kept Titus's existence hidden from Darrow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dancer, stern, speaking; Darrow beside him listening.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts to the rebel leader's choice to conceal Titus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the concealment is Dancer's decision, with his stern face.

callout.text: CRUSHED IN A MATTER OF WEEKS

storyboard.claim: A rebellion led by Titus would be crushed within weeks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dancer holding an hourglass; the sand is the short time left.
storyboard.onScreenText: CRUSHED IN A MATTER OF WEEKS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dancer's quoted warning continues.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass reads time running out, which is the speed of the crushing.

storyboard.claim: Titus's rebellion would burn hot and then die out, because no society is built on rape and murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon reads wildfire; Dancer speaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes Dancer's warning with the wildfire image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wildfire metaphor is literal fire that exhausts itself.

storyboard.claim: The gold narrative justifies their tyranny by calling the lower colors base.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator thinking; no icon for a justification.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the gold narrative from the start of the video.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls the story the Golds tell about themselves.

storyboard.claim: Titus's savage rage confirms the gold claim that reds are savages.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, angry, pointing; the accusation is in his stance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the gold narrative to Titus's behaviour.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows his rage as the evidence the Golds would point to.

storyboard.claim: If a red gets power and acts like a rabid animal, the gold claim is proven right.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Spells out the logic of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the conclusion of the trap plainly.

storyboard.claim: Titus is the worst possible representative for the red cause.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow, worried, thinking, with Titus behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the damage Titus does to the cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Darrow is shown weighing it, so the viewer sees the stakes for the cause.

callout.text: HE MUST BE BETTER THAN THE GOLDS

storyboard.claim: To win, Darrow must be fundamentally better than the Golds, not merely more violent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow thinking; no icon.
storyboard.onScreenText: HE MUST BE BETTER THAN THE GOLDS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darrow's conclusion after the Titus example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the lesson into Darrow's own resolution.

storyboard.claim: The gold story is the real cage, and Titus is trapped in it playing the savage they expect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask over Titus's face; Titus, worried, slumped and playing a role.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Titus as a prisoner of the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows he is trapped, not merely wrong.

storyboard.claim: The hosts are about to synthesize all the layers of control in the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking to camera; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition to the synthesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the synthesis the next beats will list.

storyboard.claim: The book's physical mechanics demand a large suspension of disbelief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the critique of the worldbuilding.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the critique in the book's own terms.

storyboard.claim: The premise requires a society perfectly cut off from the surface.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon reads exclusion and no way in or out; the narrator agrees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The premise the previous beat questioned.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door says the isolation is closed off on purpose.

storyboard.claim: Millions of reds have lived underground for hundreds of years with almost no leaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon for underground.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the isolation premise.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the scale, millions and centuries, in the callout.

storyboard.claim: No tech or debris from the surface city ever reaches the underground.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A city icon for the intact surface city; the narrator speaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what could have leaked and did not.
storyboard.addedInformation: The surface city stands for everything kept out.

storyboard.claim: The narrative needs flawless sensory deprivation across a planet for centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator thinking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Finishes the leak list with the ventilation shaft.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the requirement in one phrase.

storyboard.claim: A messy human society could not keep a firewall that perfect; it is a stretch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator thinking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Judges the isolation as implausible.
storyboard.addedInformation: A plain verdict on the premise's plausibility.

storyboard.claim: We accept the isolation as a necessary science fiction convention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the stretch is accepted.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the genre convention as the reason to accept it.

storyboard.claim: Brown uses the isolation to set up a philosophical lab experiment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the author's purpose for the isolation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the book as a controlled experiment.

storyboard.claim: Isolation lets the ideological cage be examined without interference.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the purpose of the lab.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says why the isolation must be absolute.

storyboard.claim: The thematic payoff justifies forgiving the worldbuilding stretch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator pointing ahead to the payoff; no icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the critique and turns to the synthesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the reason for forgiving the stretch.

storyboard.claim: The book spends its length on the terrifying arsenal of the Gold Society.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon for the arsenal; Darrow, afraid, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the list of gold power.
storyboard.addedInformation: Darrow's fear shows how the arsenal is meant to intimidate.

storyboard.claim: The gold arsenal includes razor swords, orbital fleets, grav boots and modified muscles.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator pointing at the list; no icon, since the weapons are listed rather than shown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of gold power.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the weapons the readers are meant to fear.

storyboard.claim: Readers are meant to be intimidated by the gold physical power at first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow, afraid, slumped in the hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States what the arsenal is meant to do.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the intimidation landing on the reader's proxy.

callout.text: THE ULTIMATE WEAPON IS A BEDTIME STORY

storyboard.claim: The gold society's ultimate weapon is the story it tells, not its fleets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon reads the bedtime story literally; the narrator speaks.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE ULTIMATE WEAPON IS A BEDTIME STORY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The punchline of the synthesis: the weapon is the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals the book's central claim in one image.
